listenings.text: Right, my audio profile. I am Ana and I am thirteen. On weekdays my routine is always the same: school, lunch, homework, and then I am free. I usually swim on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and once in a while I go to the pool on Saturday too, but only if my sister goes. I am quite good at swimming, actually. I hardly ever watch television, because I can't stand the commercials, so I read instead. And I never do my homework at night. Never. I always do it before dinner, or it does not get done.

A quick note about the noticeboard, because people keep asking. The board is always up to date, and I update it every Monday morning. New members join on the first Wednesday of the month, so if somebody new appears in your group, that is why. We rarely change the meeting time, but it does happen twice a year, in December and in July. And one thing that surprises people: we hardly ever cancel. In four years we have cancelled twice. So if the weather is bad, come anyway.

reading.rtitle: Three profiles from the club noticeboard
paras: MAYA, 12, Nairobi. On weekdays my routine hardly ever changes: I get up at six, and I am always at school by seven thirty. I play basketball twice a week and I am quite good at it, although I never watch it on television. I can't stand losing, which my brother says is a problem.

TOMAS, 13, Prague. I joined the club last month, so I am still the newest member. I usually ride my bike to school, but in winter I rarely take the bike out, because the roads freeze. Once in a while my father drives me, and then I am late anyway. I am good at drawing and terrible at swimming.

LEILA, 12, Marseille. I am often the last person to arrive here, and I always apologize for it. My routine is simple: school, the sea, homework, in that order. I swim every single day in summer and hardly ever in winter. I sometimes swap books with Maya by mail, which takes about three weeks each way.

gist.prompt: Which title fits the three profiles best?
choices: How to join an international club
Three routines, and how often each thing really happens
Sports you can practice in any country

items: Maya's weekday routine changes a lot.
She says her routine on weekdays hardly ever changes.
Maya plays basketball but does not watch it on television.
She plays twice a week and never watches it on television.
Tomas has been a member for a long time.
He joined last month and is still the newest member.
Tomas cycles less in winter than in the rest of the year.
In winter he rarely takes the bike out, because the roads freeze.
Leila swims the same amount all year.
She swims every single day in summer and hardly ever in winter.
Leila and Maya send books to each other.

items.situation: Somebody asks how often you play your favourite sport. Answer with an adverb and a number.
Describe your weekday routine in three sentences, each one with a different adverb of frequency.
Name one thing you can't stand, and say how often you have to do it anyway.
Somebody asks what you are good at. Answer, and say how often you practice.
Correct this out loud: "I go always to school by bus." Then say your own true version.
